item.title: BurnRate 2026: Track What You Spend on AI Coding Tools
item.description: BurnRate is a local-first AI coding cost analytics tool that tracks spend across 7+ providers, detects waste, and helps teams optimize their AI tool budgets.
item.content:encoded:
What Is BurnRate and Why Does It Matter in 2026?

BurnRate is an AI agent observability and cost analytics tool that tracks what you spend on AI coding tools across multiple providers. In 2026, as enterprises face a full-blown AI spend crisis — with Uber, Meta, Microsoft, and Walmart all capping employee AI tool usage in the same month — BurnRate solves the fundamental problem that most teams cannot answer: “How much are we actually spending on AI coding tools, and is it worth it?” The tool monitors usage across 7 major providers and 40+ models, providing the data you need to optimize your AI coding budget.

The Big Picture — Enterprise AI Spend Is Out of Control

The 2026 AI coding tools market is estimated at $4.2 billion annually, according to the BurnRate 2026 Cost Report. That figure represents spending across subscriptions, API usage, and enterprise licensing for tools like Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, Aider, Cline, and Codex CLI. The problem is that most organizations have no visibility into where that money goes.

The shift from flat-rate pricing to metered billing has caught many teams off guard. GitHub Copilot’s transition to AI Credits (token-based billing) on June 1, 2026 — where 1 credit equals $0.01 — marked a turning point. What was once a predictable $10–$39 per developer per month is now a variable cost that can spike unpredictably. One Pro+ developer burned 8% of their monthly 7,000-credit allocation in just two hours on a single complex change. Agentic Workspace sessions on Copilot cost 30 to 600+ credits each, making the cost of a single AI-assisted task highly variable.

Uber, Meta, Microsoft, Walmart: The June 2026 Cap Wave

June 2026 was a watershed month for enterprise AI cost management. Multiple Fortune 500 companies simultaneously announced spending caps and usage restrictions on AI coding tools:

Company Action Taken Details
Uber $1,500/month per-tool cap Exhausted 2026 AI budget in ~4 months; capped Cursor and Claude Code
Meta Per-employee token caps 73.7T tokens consumed in ~30 days across 85k+ employees; internal AI costs approaching billions
Microsoft License cancellations Cancelling Claude Code licenses, moving engineers to GitHub Copilot CLI
Walmart Per-employee token allowance In-house Code Puppy tool after demand outran budget
AT&T Access restrictions Limiting GitHub Copilot access for some employees
Amazon Expanded access (counter-example) Expanded Claude Code + Codex company-wide after developer pushback (1,500-endorsement thread)

The pattern is clear: enterprises that adopted AI coding tools enthusiastically in 2024–2025 are now facing the bill. Meta alone consumed 73.7 trillion tokens in approximately 30 days across 85,000+ employees, with internal AI costs approaching billions of dollars according to Fortune and The Next Web. Microsoft reported spending approximately $500 to $2,000 per engineer per month on Claude Code before deciding to cancel licenses and migrate to GitHub Copilot CLI.

From Tokenmaxxing to Tokenminimizing

The industry is undergoing a fundamental shift from “tokenmaxxing” — using as much AI as possible without regard for cost — to “tokenminimizing” — actively optimizing every AI interaction for cost efficiency. This shift is documented by the ai-spend-cap-tracker project on GitHub, which tracks organizations capping employee AI coding spend in 2026.

The tokenminimizing mindset means:

  • Measuring ROI per AI interaction rather than assuming all AI usage is valuable
  • Choosing the right model for each task instead of defaulting to the most capable (and expensive) model
  • Monitoring context window efficiency — you may be billed for 1M tokens but only getting 200K–300K of usable context
  • Tracking waste patterns like ghost agents, bloated configurations, and unused MCP servers

BurnRate Deep Dive — Features and Capabilities

BurnRate positions itself as the leading commercial solution for AI coding cost analytics. It offers a comprehensive feature set designed for individual developers, teams, and enterprises.

Multi-Provider Tracking (7+ AI Coding Tools)

BurnRate tracks usage across seven major AI coding tools and 40+ models in a single dashboard. This includes Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, Aider, Cline, and Codex CLI. Instead of logging into separate provider dashboards — many of which offer limited cost breakdowns — you get a unified view of all AI coding spend.

The tool refreshes pricing data from LiteLLM daily, ensuring cost calculations reflect the latest model pricing changes. This is critical in a market where providers adjust pricing frequently to compete.

Sub-Agent Observability

One of BurnRate’s standout features is sub-agent visibility. When an AI coding tool spawns sub-agents to complete complex tasks, those sub-agents generate their own token usage and API calls. Neither Anthropic nor OpenAI provide visibility into sub-agent costs in their native dashboards. BurnRate fills this gap by tracking the full agent tree, giving you a complete picture of what each task actually costs.

This matters because agentic workflows are becoming the norm. A single task that spawns 5–10 sub-agents can cost 5–10x more than a simple chat interaction, and without sub-agent observability, those costs are invisible.

Optimization Engine with 23 Rules

BurnRate includes 23 actionable optimization rules designed to reduce AI coding costs by up to 40%, according to the tool’s documentation on OpenAlt. These rules detect common waste patterns:

  • Ghost agents: AI processes running in the background consuming tokens without producing value
  • Bloated configurations: Overly permissive model selections that default to expensive models for simple tasks
  • Unused MCP servers: Model Context Protocol servers that are connected but never used, still consuming resources
  • Context window waste: Sending unnecessarily large context that exceeds what the model can effectively use
  • Redundant tool calls: Multiple tools performing the same function, duplicating costs

Each optimization rule comes with an estimated savings potential, allowing teams to prioritize the highest-impact changes first.

Local-First Architecture and Privacy

BurnRate operates with a local-first architecture, meaning all cost data stays on your machine. There is no cloud dependency, which is a significant advantage for organizations with strict data privacy requirements. The tool is free for individual developers, making it accessible for freelancers and students who need to monitor their AI spending without committing to a paid plan.

The local-first approach also means no data leaves your network, addressing concerns about sending proprietary code metadata or usage patterns to third-party servers. This is particularly important for enterprises in regulated industries like finance, healthcare, and defense.

PDF Reports and Rate Limit Monitoring

BurnRate can generate professional PDF reports suitable for sharing with management or finance teams. This is a practical feature for engineering leads who need to justify AI tool budgets to stakeholders. The reports include spend breakdowns by tool, model, project, and team member.

Rate limit monitoring is another practical feature. BurnRate tracks your usage against provider rate limits and alerts you before you hit a cap, preventing service interruptions during critical development work. This is especially valuable for teams using free or lower-tier plans with strict rate limits.

BurnRate Pricing — Free, Pro, Team, Enterprise

BurnRate offers a tiered pricing model:

Tier Price Key Features
Free $0 Individual developer, local-first, basic tracking
Pro Paid Advanced analytics, optimization engine, PDF reports
Team Paid Multi-user collaboration, shared dashboards, team budgets
Enterprise Custom SSO, audit logs, dedicated support, custom integrations

The free tier is notably generous — individual developers get full local-first functionality at no cost. Advanced features like the optimization engine, PDF reports, and team collaboration require paid tiers. The tool’s OpenAlt score of 38/100 reflects its positioning as a niche tool rather than a general-purpose analytics platform.

How BurnRate Compares to Alternatives

BurnRate is not the only AI coding cost tracker on the market. Here is how it stacks up against the main alternatives.

BurnRate vs CodeBurn (Open-Source Alternative)

CodeBurn is a free, open-source, local-first AI coding cost tracker that supports 36 AI tools and agents — significantly more than BurnRate’s 7. It offers unique features like the One-Shot Rate metric (measuring how often AI gets edits right on the first try) and an optimize command that detects waste patterns. CodeBurn runs as a macOS menu bar app, desktop app, and terminal dashboard, supporting 162 currencies.

Feature BurnRate CodeBurn
Tools tracked 7 36
Price Free (individual) / Paid (team) Free, open-source
Architecture Local-first Local-first
One-Shot Rate No Yes
PDF Reports Yes No
Team collaboration Yes (paid) No
Currencies Limited 162
Platform Desktop app macOS menu bar, desktop, terminal

Verdict: CodeBurn is better for individual developers who want maximum tool coverage and don’t need team features. BurnRate is better for teams and enterprises that need collaboration, reporting, and support.

BurnRate vs ai-spend-cap-tracker (Community Tracker)

The ai-spend-cap-tracker is not a tool but a community-maintained GitHub repository that documents organizations capping employee AI coding spend in 2026. It serves as a public record of the enterprise AI spend crisis, tracking companies like Uber, Meta, Microsoft, Walmart, and AT&T.

Feature BurnRate ai-spend-cap-tracker
Purpose Cost tracking & optimization Public documentation of caps
Active tool Yes No (read-only tracker)
Optimization 23 rules None
Community Commercial Open-source community
Best for Managing your spend Understanding industry trends

Verdict: These are complementary. Use BurnRate to manage your own AI spend; use ai-spend-cap-tracker to understand what other companies are doing and benchmark your policies.

BurnRate vs aiburnrate.com (Claude Code Focus)

aiburnrate.com is a specialized tool focused specifically on Claude Code cost tracking. While BurnRate covers multiple providers, aiburnrate.com goes deeper on Claude Code-specific metrics and optimization.

Feature BurnRate aiburnrate.com
Provider coverage 7 tools Claude Code only
Depth Broad Deep (Claude-specific)
Best for Multi-tool teams Claude Code power users

Verdict: If your team uses only Claude Code, aiburnrate.com may offer more depth. If you use multiple AI coding tools, BurnRate’s unified dashboard is more valuable.

The GitHub Copilot Credit Shock — Why You Need a Tracker Now

GitHub Copilot’s transition to AI Credits on June 1, 2026, represents one of the most significant pricing changes in the AI coding tools market. The new billing structure is:

  • Copilot Pro ($10/month): 1,500 credits
  • Copilot Pro+ ($39/month): 7,000 credits
  • Copilot Max ($100/month): 20,000 credits

With 1 credit equal to $0.01, the math is straightforward but the usage patterns are not. A single Agentic Workspace session can cost 30 to 600+ credits ($0.30 to $6.00+). One developer on a Pro+ plan burned 8% of their monthly allocation in two hours on a single complex change. At that rate, a team of 10 developers doing complex agentic work could exhaust their Pro+ allocation in under two weeks.

This is why a burnrate AI coding spend tracker is no longer optional. Without tracking, you cannot:

  • Predict monthly costs under the new credit system
  • Identify which developers or tasks are consuming the most credits
  • Set budgets and alerts before costs spiral
  • Compare the ROI of different AI coding tools

Real-World Use Cases

Freelancers Tracking Client Project Costs

For freelancers using AI coding tools across multiple client projects, BurnRate provides project-level cost breakdowns. This allows accurate billing and helps determine whether AI tool costs should be passed through to clients or absorbed as a business expense. The free tier is sufficient for most freelancers.

Engineering Teams Managing AI Budgets

Engineering teams with 5–100 developers face the most complex cost management challenges. With multiple team members using different tools at different intensities, costs can vary wildly month to month. BurnRate’s team tier provides shared dashboards, budget alerts, and per-developer spend breakdowns that help engineering leads manage AI tool budgets proactively.

Solopreneurs Optimizing Multi-Tool Spend

Solopreneurs often use multiple AI coding tools for different aspects of their workflow — Claude Code for complex reasoning, Cursor for rapid prototyping, Copilot for everyday coding. BurnRate’s unified dashboard helps identify which tools provide the best ROI and whether subscription costs justify the value received.

Pros and Cons of BurnRate

Pros Cons
Tracks 7 major AI coding tools in one dashboard No cloud sync — data is local only
Sub-agent visibility unavailable from providers No team collaboration on free tier
23 optimization rules with up to 40% savings No API or CLI for CI/CD integration
Local-first architecture ensures data privacy Advanced features locked behind paid tiers
Free for individual developers Limited to 7 tools vs CodeBurn’s 36
PDF reports for management/finance OpenAlt score of 38/100 (niche tool)
Rate limit monitoring prevents interruptions Requires local installation

Who Is BurnRate Best For?

BurnRate is best suited for:

  • Engineering teams (5–50 developers) who need visibility into multi-tool AI spend and want team collaboration features
  • Individual developers who use multiple AI coding tools and want a free, local-first cost tracker
  • Freelancers who need project-level cost breakdowns for client billing
  • Enterprises in regulated industries that require local-first data privacy

BurnRate is less suitable for:

  • Developers using only one AI tool — a specialized tracker may offer more depth
  • Teams needing cloud sync — BurnRate’s local-first design means no cross-device data sharing
  • CI/CD pipeline cost tracking — no API or CLI integration available

Final Verdict — Is BurnRate Worth It in 2026?

The 2026 AI coding tools market is at an inflection point. With enterprise spend reaching $4.2 billion annually, major companies capping usage, and GitHub Copilot’s shift to metered billing, the need for a burnrate AI coding spend tracker has never been greater.

BurnRate addresses a genuine and urgent problem: most teams have no idea what they are spending on AI coding tools. The tool’s multi-provider tracking, sub-agent observability, and 23 optimization rules provide actionable insights that can reduce costs by up to 40%. The local-first architecture is a strong privacy advantage, and the free tier makes it accessible to individual developers.

However, BurnRate is not without limitations. The 7-tool coverage is narrower than CodeBurn’s 36-tool support. The lack of cloud sync and team collaboration on the free tier may frustrate some users. And the OpenAlt score of 38/100 suggests the tool is still maturing.

For engineering teams managing multi-tool AI spend in 2026, BurnRate is worth trying — especially on the free tier. The optimization engine alone can pay for the tool many times over. But for individual developers who want maximum tool coverage at zero cost, CodeBurn’s open-source approach may be a better fit.

FAQ

What is BurnRate and how does it track AI coding costs?

BurnRate is an AI agent observability and cost analytics tool that tracks spending across 7 major AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf, Aider, Cline, Codex CLI) and 40+ models. It provides a unified dashboard showing spend by tool, model, project, and task, with daily refreshed pricing from LiteLLM.

Is BurnRate free to use?

Yes, BurnRate is free for individual developers with its local-first basic tracking tier. Advanced features like the optimization engine, PDF reports, and team collaboration require paid Pro, Team, or Enterprise plans.

How does BurnRate compare to CodeBurn?

BurnRate supports 7 tools with team collaboration and PDF reporting, while CodeBurn supports 36 tools as a free open-source alternative. BurnRate is better for teams; CodeBurn is better for individual developers wanting maximum tool coverage.

Can BurnRate help reduce my AI coding costs?

Yes, BurnRate includes 23 optimization rules that detect waste patterns like ghost agents, bloated configurations, and unused MCP servers. The tool claims potential savings of up to 40% through these optimizations.

Does BurnRate work offline or require cloud connectivity?

BurnRate uses a local-first architecture, meaning all cost data stays on your machine with no cloud dependency. This ensures data privacy but means no cross-device sync or cloud backup on the free tier.
